subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a nine-tailed kitsune fox model with spirit flames in a high-fantasy anime style, thinking through which builder utilities I'll need for the geometry and effects since I won't be able to test interactively.

I'm sketching the design: a white-furred fox with crimson kitsune markings, nine fanned tails, glowing anime eyes, and floating blue-violet spirit flames, standing on a small rune-etched stone shrine platform, with the fox sized around 0.8m at the shoulder. Now I'm working out the skeleton coordinates for a quadruped stance, defining the hips, spine chain, and chest positions to build the body structure.

Next I'm mapping out the neck and head joints extending forward from the chest, then planning how to sweep the body mesh along the spine path, considering whether to use separate sweeps for the torso and neck while being careful about seams where they overlap.

Continuing the body path points through chest and up toward the neck, with spine covering the rear portion and neck the front, then working out a radius function that tapers appropriately from rump to head.

Finishing the body radius function...

Now I'm thinking about the four legs with inverse kinematics, placing shoulder and foot targets for the front legs, and planning the fox's coloring with slender legs, dark sock markings, and white kitsune fur with a crimson accent.

For coloring I'm settling on cream-white fur with cel-shading using a lavender-shifted shadow tone, crimson vermilion facial markings in a kumadori style, dark inked paws, and glowing cyan-violet spirit flames for contrast.

Writing fur shading logic...

Now moving to the tails: planning nine tails fanning out from the rump, each built as a chain of about four joints.

Working out each tail's spread angle from center, with root at the rump and curving backward and upward, tapering fluffy radius from thin at base to thick mid-length then pointed tip, with a white flame-tipped end.

Still writing tail curve math...

Still naming tail joint chains...

Now I'm working out the tail's taper profile, attaching it to the hips with four joints and shaping a radius function that swells near the base and narrows to a point at the tip.

Adding tail tip color logic...

Now I'm setting up the head joint position, placing it forward and slightly up from the neck chain, aiming the head direction slightly downward-forward.

For the head itself, I'm thinking through skull and muzzle shapes, a black nose, separate lower jaw, pointed ears with dark inner tufts, spiky cheek ruffs, and custom slit-shaped fox eyes with vermilion eyeliner rather than using a generic anime eye decal.

Writing decal projection code...

Now I'm working out the head geometry itself: placing the skull center and radii, tapering a sweep for the snout from a wider base to a narrow tip, adding a small dark nose sphere, and setting up the jaw joint with its own sweep for the lower jaw.

I'll skip posing the jaw for now and keep the mouth closed, simpler and safer. For ears, I'm designing a pointed triangular outline to extrude upward from the head, sharp-tipped for a classic ear shape.

Computing the extrusion axes...

Working out the exact offset so the inner ear pokes out slightly past the outer ear's front face without breaking through the back, keeping it independent of the thickness axis. I'll mirror the outline for symmetry, color the inner ear dark red, and consider a separate black or vermilion tip piece layered onto the outer ear.

Instead of a separate tip mesh, I'll paint the ear surface conditionally based on height so anything above a threshold becomes the tip color and the rest stays the base coat, extruding from the outline coordinates. I also need to figure out ear tilt for an outward lean, and sketch zigzag cheek ruff tufts as flame-like polygons extruded on each side of the face.

Writing outline coordinates...

For the chest ruff I'll scatter fluffy white tuft cards on the front-lower body surface. Now moving to the legs: planning front shoulder joint and foot target positions for a digitigrade quadruped stance.

Checking that the segment lengths sum to roughly cover the vertical drop from shoulder to ground, with a slight bend so the elbow angles back and the wrist angles forward for a slender fox-like front leg.

For the hind leg, setting hip root and foot target positions, then choosing digitigrade segment lengths (thigh, shin, metatarsal) that overshoot the vertical reach slightly so the knee bends forward and the hock bends back naturally.

Naming each joint chain (shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw for front, hip/knee/hock/foot for hind) with L/R suffixes based on side, then placing foot targets near ground level and adding paw geometry at the tip joints. I'm also varying sweep radii along each limb, thicker at the top and tapering down, plus adding a separate haunch ellipsoid for the hind thigh.

Adding toe bumps to paws...

For kitsune flair, I'm thinking of adding a shimenawa rope with paper shide streamers around the neck instead of claws, plus maybe a bell or tassel, placing it as a loop around the neck joint.

Also adding a glowing cyan magatama pendant shaped like a tapering comma swept along an arc, plus crimson kumadori-style facial markings as a decal at the forehead and cheeks. For the base, I'll use a lathed octagonal stone platform.

But now I realize the fox needs to stand on y=0, so if I add a base slab, I either need to shift every body coordinate up by the base height or sink the feet into the base so the model's lowest point still touches the floor — I'll go with recessing the paws into the base to avoid recalculating every number.

With base height G=0.1, paws touch the top of the base and the lathe runs y 0..G so tails don't hang. Now I'm thinking through the spirit flames — a ring of nine hitodama orbs around the fox, each one a glowing teardrop flame shape, possibly built as an extrusion with bevel and a cyan glow, maybe combined with a textured cross-card for extra brightness.

Still writing flame outline points...

Closing the path back to the start completes the valid polygon, so I'll keep smoothing at 1 for a soft tip and double-check that corner-cutting near the narrow spike doesn't create self-intersections with the neighboring edges.

Now I'm thinking about the inner flame wisp—a lighter white-cyan layer scaled down and slightly raised with a glow, and whether to orient the extruded flames radially outward or use crossing extrudes at 90° so they read well from multiple viewing angles despite being thin edge-on.

I'm planning the hitodama's overall composition: nine orbiting flames spiraling at varying radius and height, a glowing rune ring on the base, and tiny ember sparks made from small icosahedra, weighing whether to merge those embers into groups for efficiency while keeping the total part count within a reasonable range.

I realize octahedron geometry is non-indexed, so merging would need consistent non-indexed data, but since it'd lose flat coloring anyway I decide to skip merging and just keep the embers as roughly 28 separate parts. I'm also figuring out how the floating flames should attach to the skeleton, considering whether to just let them snap to the nearest existing joint or instead create a dedicated joint near the root to anchor the spirit ring.

I'll add a "flameRing" joint parented to hips so the flames can spin independently. For the base, I'm designing a lathed octagonal stone platform with a wider lower disk and a raised inner step, giving it dimensions around 1.25 radius tapering to 1.0, with a mottled stone-and-moss paint treatment.

For the top surface, I'm planning a rune circle using concentric rings and nine flame glyphs, drawn as simple stroke-based tick marks and a nine-pointed star rather than actual text, keeping it lightweight to render.

Writing SVG path code...

Thinking about whether to add a small torii gate or stone lantern as background detail -- maybe a pair of torii pillars behind the tail fan, needing to adjust base disc size and placement so it doesn't clash with the fox's silhouette.

Base radius 1.6 feels acceptable for the overall scale, though I want the torii to stay modest so it doesn't overshadow the fox — I'll pull the tail tips back to around z=-0.9 and keep the torii pillars thin, about 2.0 high, painted vermilion with a black top beam.

I'm also considering adding a pair of stone lanterns flanking the front with glowing windows for extra charm — each built from a base, post, glow box, roof, and finial, placed symmetrically on the base. Running a rough part count now: body around 40, legs with paws and toes about 30, and tails still need tallying up.

Tallying up remaining totals — legs, tails, head, ruff, torii, lanterns, flames, embers, base, rune, moss — landing around 220 parts total. Now thinking through the texture list: eye SVG, forehead decal mark, rune circle, paper talisman or hang tag, fur tuft cards, and a torii plaque — though I'm wary of rendering CJK glyphs directly via SVG text since font support could fail, so I'll draw the kanji shape manually instead.

Settling on a plaque texture showing a fox-head/nine-tail emblem built from paths like a nine-pointed star, plus a flame icon for the lantern window glow, and grass blade cards scattered around the base edges. Final texture count comes to about eight: eye, mark, rune, tuft, plaque, lantern window, grass, and ofuda.

Starting the implementation now, being conservative with the API since I can't test as I go. Writing imports...

Defining color palette...

I'm also setting up the skeleton structure, starting with the hips as the root spine joint, positioned and oriented to anchor the rest of the body hierarchy.

Still building the joint chain...

Defining the body sweep path...

I'm deciding the bone list should just use spine and neck since the rump segment naturally resolves to the hips/spine joint. For coloring, I'm keeping the body mostly white and adding a cream-colored belly marking using a fur edge effect to soften the transition.

Now I'm also adding crimson flame-swirl decals on the haunches and shoulders, kitsune-style tomoe emblems, placing them near the hip and shoulder surfaces with small decal sizes.

I'm setting up an ellipsoid haunch piece per side as a separate scaled sphere part, positioned near the hip joint, so the flame decal can target it directly. Now I'm writing the leg construction loop...

Defining chain joint names and contact points...

I'm adding small sphere toes to the front paws, then moving to the hind leg setup — placing hip and foot joints for a digitigrade stance with segment lengths and bend directions, checking the resulting joint distances.

Still working through the hind leg IK, positioning the hock-to-foot segment vertically and placing the hind paw ellipsoid slightly forward of the foot target so the toes point forward. I'm verifying the leg radius tapers enough at the bottom to stay covered by the paw, then setting up the chain parenting for the hind legs off the hips.

Now I'm naming joints consistently: hip/knee/hock/foot for hind legs, shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw for front legs, making sure each is unique per side. I'm also placing the haunch sphere at the hip joint.

Moving to head geometry, I'm defining the skull center and radii in fox-space coordinates so it extends forward from the neck joint, then starting the sphere geometry for the skull part.

Then I'm defining the muzzle as a tapered sweep from the skull forward, shrinking its radius along the way using an interpolation function.

I'm placing a small ink-colored nose sphere at the muzzle tip, then starting on the lower jaw by attaching a jaw joint to the head bone.

Now I'm checking the jaw sweep geometry against the muzzle underside to make sure the lower jaw sits below the upper muzzle rather than overlapping it, adjusting the vertical positions so the jaw reads as distinct from the snout above it.

I'll add a small dark box for the mouth line to suggest a gap, plus two tiny downward-pointing cone fangs on the upper jaw. Cheeks get extruded tufts, and I'm planning eye placement as decals near the front of the skull.

Computing the skull surface position at that eye location works out to roughly (s*0.08, 1.15, 0.67), orienting the decal direction outward and slightly down, with a wide oval shape sized for an 80:40 aspect ratio.

Figuring out which eye gets the wing accent: the model's left eye (s=+1) should mirror when drawn so the wing points toward the outer corner correctly from the viewer's perspective. Now I'm sketching the SVG eye shape itself, starting with the almond outline and crimson liner wing paths.

Writing SVG gradient code...

Still writing eye details...

Now I'm designing a forehead facemark decal: a crimson diamond/teardrop shape positioned on the skull's upper front, accented with a gold dot, meant to echo kitsune-style markings swooping back from the eyes.

Writing paint logic for ears and tufts...

I'm considering whether to skip color tinting and instead add tuft cards along the tails for a fluffy, flame-like edge, scattering around 36 cards across each of 9 tails with lean and flow oriented outward along the tail direction.

Now I'm sketching a shimenawa rope around the neck, using a skin loop anchored on a neck joint with a direction and lift, letting it wrap around partway down the neck.

For the rope's appearance, I'm giving it a straw-like grain texture with twisted stripe coloring, computing a paint function that alternates bands based on position along the path and the twist angle to simulate braided strands.

I should double check the modulo math handles wraparound cleanly, and confirm the loop plane for the neck cut actually passes through the joint perpendicular to its axis so it takes the smallest cross-sectional ring at that point on the body surface.

Now I'm adding the shide, the zigzag paper streamers hanging from the rope — placing three along the rope path with the paper extruded downward using a jagged lightning-bolt outline shape.

Closing the shide outline and checking it doesn't self-intersect, I decide to place four of these paper strips evenly around the rope loop, oriented so each one faces outward along the tangent direction of the circular path rather than edge-on.

For the pendant, I'm thinking of a teardrop shape made from a swept catmull path tapering toward a point, wrapped in a glow effect, and positioned hanging from the front of the rope at the neck using a nearest-point lookup on the rope's surface.

I'm placing a magatama-shaped pendant below the neck point, building its curled outline with a sweep that tapers from a thick head to a thin tail, rigidly attached to the neck bone. No extra ring ornament needed at the hip or tail base.

Now I'm computing the fan of tails, looping through nine positions spread by angle, each with root, mid, and tip control points curving outward and back from the body to form the characteristic splayed fox tail shape.

Computing the tail points...

Tuning the tail radius curve...

I'm writing a flame-generating function that places small glowing flames at each tail tip, scaled and colored in violet/cyan, attached to the last tail joint.

Still defining flame geometry...

Working out placement math to keep the orbit flames spread across the front arc so they don't collide with the tail flames or torii pillars in the back region.

I'm checking that the flame near the fox's chest stays small and low enough not to overlap it, then double-checking spacing between the lanterns and nearby flames so their heights and positions don't collide.

I notice a conflict at φ=±101 with the lantern position, so I'm adjusting the flame orbit radius inward to 0.95 and restricting the angular range to ±110° to avoid overlapping the fox's tail at the back, stepping by 27.5° across nine positions.

Now I'm checking the lanterns against the base radius and torii pillars—with pillars at x=±1.0 and height 2.15, the base needs to extend to about 1.75 to clear everything, and the tail tips plus flame height still fit comfortably within that boundary.

I'll make the base a two-tier platform, with a rune circle glowing in green/cyan for contrast against the fox's white fur. For the torii gate, I'm building the pillars as rounded wooden rods in vermillion with flat octagonal ends, plus a black base ring where each pillar meets the ground.

Now I'm adding the connecting beam (nuki) between the pillars, and shaping the top crossbeam (kasagi) with a slightly upward-curved profile at the ends, extruding a custom polygon outline to get that classic torii silhouette.

Working out pillar and shimaki heights so the torii totals about 2.33 units tall with the fox's tails ending around 1.75. I'm also adding a plaque between the nuki and shimaki, positioned with a texture-mapped front face.

Setting up the torii so it faces forward toward the viewer, with vermilion grain-textured paint on the pillars and nuki. Now I'm sketching lantern geometry near the base using a hexagonal lathed profile...

Still building the lanterns...

Still defining stone paint colors, then I'll scatter grass card decorations around the base edges using mirrored lantern positions and a rune circle, filtering scatter hits by surface normal and radius to place blade-shaped grass billboards.

Defining the inner ear outline...

Simplifying the ear paint threshold to a basic color split. Then thinking about adding a golden forehead circlet with a cyan gem as a decorative crown element, planning to build it as a ring loop cut around the skull on a tilted plane near the forehead.

Actually reconsidering the circlet idea since the ring would wrap oddly around the whole head rather than sitting as a tiara. Settling instead on a simpler golden forehead ornament: keep the crimson flame mark decal but add a small glowing cyan octahedron gem at its center, set in gold.

I'm computing the forehead hit point using the skull surface's angular coordinates (front direction, elevated 55°), then placing the decal there with its orientation, and embedding the glowing gem stick slightly above it so it sits naturally on top of the mark.

For body decals, I'm adding flame swirl marks on the haunch and shoulder using a crimson comma-flame SVG path, positioning them on the haunch surface based on the sphere's radius offset, and mirroring the swirl direction depending on left/right side.

I'm also sizing a shoulder blob to match the shoulder joint, applying the same flame decal there for consistency, and setting up chest fluff by scattering white fur cards in the front-neck region where the surface normal points forward and the z-coordinate falls within the chest band.

Now I'm defining the body's fur edge with a jagged, toothed pattern along the belly seam blending a cream and rose tone for the underside, making sure the body sweep rounds off cleanly at the rump. For the face, I'm leaving the brow and eyes as already handled, and adding a few thin cream whisker rods extending outward from the muzzle on each side.

For the paws, I'm writing a helper function that builds each paw as an ellipsoid with three toe spheres positioned slightly forward and spaced across the front, colored with a darker sock tone, skipping claws for simplicity. I'm also planning small flame accents licking at the tail tips and a couple of wisps near the shoulders alongside the orbiting hitodama, plus a scattering of small ember particles to finish the spirit-fox effect.

I'm scattering those embers randomly through a cylindrical volume around the fox using a seeded RNG, glowing cyan, violet, and gold, keeping their radius beyond the body so they don't intersect the fur or tails. I'm also sketching out the joint hierarchy for a flame ring attached near the hips and a base joint at the origin to anchor the whole rig.

Still designing the rune texture...

Designing the plaque texture with a dark indigo rounded rect, gold border, and a nine-petal emblem of curved tails fanning from a center point in gold. Also sketching a lantern window texture with a warm gradient background.

Now I'm drafting grass and tuft textures: a three-blade grass shape in green gradients, and a lavender-stroked white blade shape for the tuft, adjusting the curve so the root sits broad at the bottom edge of the frame.

Skipping kumadori facial stripe decals for now, I'm moving on to writing the full code file with imports from the toon kit for builders, randomization, curve utilities, limbs, painting, and fur edges.

Setting up imports...

Writing color palette and vertex helpers...

For hind legs I'll reuse the same sock level logic, just adjusted higher. Then I'm working out the tail paint function, which colors the tip vermillion past a zigzag boundary around 76% along the tail, with teeth frequency tuned to the circumference, and considering adding a cream band just inside that edge for extra detail.

Now I'm sweeping the body path through catmull-rom control points along the spine, applying the coat color and a tapered profile with a round cap at the tail end and flat cap at the neck, while checking that the flat cap stays hidden inside the skull geometry at the join.

I'm worried the flat end cap of the neck might poke out as a visible disc near the skull, so instead I'll switch to a round cap and extend the body path with a few more points so the neck blends smoothly into the head without any hard edges showing.

I should include the head as a joint in the bone list alongside spine and neck so the skull deforms correctly during head turns, even though the slight mismatch in rest pose is acceptable. Now I'm defining the radius function along the body path, tapering down to about 0.055 near the neck's end.

Checking values: at t=0 the radii come out to roughly rx=.106, ry=.135, and at t=1 they shrink to rx=.055, ry=.075, with the chest peaking around t=.36 giving width .28 and depth .38.

I should dial back the max ry since .19 makes the chest too deep for a stylized fox — reducing to .165 depth works better. I'll place haunches and shoulder blobs as scaled spheres positioned relative to the body center, then move on to legs, tail, and head geometry next.

For the tail, I'm adding a small white "fluff cap" sphere at the rump to cover the tail roots cleanly. Now I'm working through the chain/parent structure for the skeleton — setting joint parents, naming the leg chains, and checking how contact points and sweeps are specified so the leg geometry follows the joint chains properly. I still need to verify how the skull's scale array should be defined.

For the eyes, I'm placing a decal on the skull surface, projecting it along an outward normal direction angled slightly up and back so it sits correctly on the side of the head, with the tilt already baked into the drawn texture so no extra roll adjustment is needed.

I'm checking if the eye quad might extend past the skull's narrower side radius near the muzzle, and considering shrinking the eye to around 0.07x0.036 and shifting it inward to x=0.065 so it stays fully on the surface for a clean projection.

I'm now finding the eye position overlaps the muzzle's top region, since the muzzle starts too wide there. I'll redesign the muzzle to start further forward with smaller radii, pulling its top edge down to avoid colliding with the eye placement.

Checking the jaw-muzzle overlap confirms the mouth line closes properly where they meet, so I'm moving on to figuring out the dark mouth interior shading.

Instead I'll add a hidden interior plate for the mouth and a small tongue as a box bone on the jaw, plus a nose sphere positioned at the muzzle tip. Then I'm placing whisker rods extending outward from the muzzle sides.

Adding whiskers, cheek tufts...

Still placing shide around the ring, using the path's tangent as the horizontal axis so each paper strip faces radially outward with the world-up vector as its default orientation.

Skipping bells and ofuda chains for now and moving to flame shapes. I'm sketching a parametric flame outline with a sharp point near the top, scaled by a factor k, and double-checking that the polygon stays simple without self-intersecting edges.

Satisfied the cut distances work for the remaining corners, I'm now drafting the flame-shape helper function, figuring out how to type the bone parameter by referencing the joint type already defined earlier in the build closure.

I'm checking that the inner flame's larger thickness makes it poke through the outer one for the crossing effect, and confirming the bevel stays within the capped-at-half-thickness constraint for both layers.

Working out the k scale factor from height, then deciding on alternating cyan/violet colors for outer and inner flame layers. I'm placing upright flames at the tail tip positions like floating hitodama, which should give a nice candle-flame effect at the ends of the tails.

Now I'm scattering embers around the ring using small octahedron glow particles at randomized angles, radii, and heights, cycling through gold, cyan, and violet colors with a seeded random function for reproducibility.

I need to exclude ember placement in the fox's tail region to avoid overlap, skipping positions where the volume intersects the tails, and keeping embers clear of the torii pillars by bounding the radius appropriately. Then I'm starting on the base lathe geometry for the shrine structure.

Writing lathe profile...

For the base coloring, I'm layering a mottled stone scale pattern as the underlying paint, then adding a moss overlay with higher contrast so patches of green show through the stone texture.

I should also think through texel density for the overall paint atlas, since the base is large and shares the same 1024-2048 sheet as the fox and torii. Rough math puts it around 5mm per texel, which seems workable, though I may want a 4096 atlas if everything doesn't fit comfortably.

Writing torii pillar code...

Still building torii pieces...

Checking the torii-to-fox framing from the camera angle looks right. Now I'm building the stone lanterns on either side using lathe geometry for the mottled stone base, then adding posts rising from the base.

Still writing lantern geometry...

I'll go with an 8-sided cylinder lantern with a repeating pane texture, keeping roof, platform, base, and post all octagonal for consistency, then top it with a small sphere finial and an inner glow for the flame.

For grass, I'm scattering cards onto the lathe-built base surface, filtering by surface normal and radius to place them on the lower tier ring and near the torii/lantern zones without overlap issues.

Now I'm setting up tail tuft cards, scattering hit points along the tail sweep surface and configuring their size, lean, and bend to create a tufted texture.

I'm working out how the cards should face relative to flow direction—using the tail tangent vector so fur grows toward the tail tip rather than flowing awkwardly backward, which should give it that fluffy, natural look from the viewing angle.

Since cards are thin edge-on from certain angles, I need `cross:true` so they're visible from the sides too, keeping triangle budget reasonable (around 10k total). I'm settling on lean 55, bend 20, cross true, 28 cards per tail, and I still need to figure out how to keep the white tuft coloring away from the vermilion tip region by filtering based on distance from the tip.

I'll measure distance from each hit point to the tip vector (tailPts[3]) and exclude anything within 0.3 units, since the hit frame carries an `at` position I can use directly. Surface scatter should perform fine here and correctly rejects points buried inside other meshes, so I can move on to the tail-tip flame effect for each tail.

Now I'm tallying up the full part count across the model: body, haunches, shoulders, legs with paws and toes, tails with their flame extrusions and cards, then the head assembly (skull, muzzle, jaw, nose, tongue, fangs, ears, cheeks, whiskers, decals, gem), plus the rope, shide, magatama, chest cards, orbiting flames, embers, base elements, and torii components — getting a rough total to make sure nothing's missing before I finalize the build.

I'm also weighing some extra ornamental touches to consider adding: small gold rings or torus shapes at the tail bases, ear ornaments with tiny gems, or a hanging bell from the rope, while deciding whether these additions are worth the extra part count or should stay simple.

Now I'm moving on to the body markings decal step, then preparing to write the final build function, setting up the builder structure with proper typing and bone attachments for each part.

Writing skeleton joints...

Writing limb chain definitions...

Checking toe placement so they protrude correctly from the paw base, and deciding to skip claw details for simplicity. I'm setting up eye textures as SVG strings created at build time, then using a decal helper to project them onto the skull surface following bone weights. For the paper shide strips, I'm placing several extruded pieces along the rope loop using an `along` helper that distributes frames evenly, with each strip's thickness, size, and paper color defined from an outline shape, making sure the tangent direction at each frame works correctly even if the loop plane is slanted. Now I'm moving on to think about eye and forehead mark decals, which will need mirroring to apply symmetrically.

For the forehead mark itself, I'm computing a point on the skull surface using an elevation/azimuth lookup from a center point, then placing a decal there oriented by the surface normal with a reasonable up vector, plus a small glowing octahedron gem embedded at the mark's center to act as a jewel, all sized proportionally to sit naturally on the forehead.

Still defining tail geometry and sweep thickness...

Still scattering cards and adding tail flame effects...

Still writing flame placement...

Setting up the rod helper signature for bones, then writing whisker placement...

Confirming skull decals come before body assembly and rope. Adding a jaw tongue box part, checking it stays hidden inside the jaw sweep geometry.
